original_question: Does the fundamental biquandle classify virtual links up to mirror images; are there informative examples of weak biquandles that are not strong; and what further structure can be extracted from the algebra with generators A and B and relation [B,(A - 1)(A, B)] = 0 associated with the linear case?
target_in_paper: Section 7, item 10, The Fundamental Biquandle, on page 23, with notation and scope supplied by Section 3.2 (Biquandles) and Section 3.3 (The Alexander Biquandle). ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly captures all three subquestions that the paper actually asks under Problem 10, and it keeps close to the paper's wording: whether the fundamental biquandle classifies virtual links up to mirror images, whether there are good examples of weak biquandles that are not strong, and what more can be understood about the two-generator algebra with relation [B,(A - 1)(A, B)] = 0 associated to the linear case. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))
missing_details: The draft should identify the problem as the specific three-part open problem in Section 7, item 10, rather than as a broader biquandle program. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))

To be stand-alone, it should specify that the invariant in question is the fundamental biquandle BQ(K), formed from a virtual link diagram by taking one generator for each edge and two relations at each crossing, and that this construction is invariant under the generalized Reidemeister moves for virtual knots and links. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))

The mirror-image clause needs the paper's exact caveat: the authors only say they know the biquandle has the same value on the orientation-reversed mirror image where the mirror is perpendicular to the plane. That caveat should be retained rather than replaced by a looser phrase such as simply 'up to mirror images.' ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))

The paper does not define 'weak biquandle' explicitly here, so a stand-alone restatement should make clear that 'strong' means the elements x, y, z, t in axiom (3) are uniquely determined; correspondingly, 'weak' means a biquandle satisfying the axioms without that uniqueness requirement. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))

The draft should tie the phrase 'linear case' to the paper's linear/Alexander biquandle context: the Alexander biquandle is presented as a linear biquandle structure on a module over Z[s, s^-1, t, t^-1]. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))

If the algebraic clause is unpacked, the cited source [5] adds hypotheses not stated in your draft: A and B are invertible, non-commuting elements of a ring R, A - 1 is also invertible, and the relation [B,(A - 1)(A, B)] = 0 is the 'fundamental equation' defining the relevant algebraic representation. ([eudml.org](https://eudml.org/doc/283165))

To stay paper-faithful, 'informative examples' should be tightened back to the paper's 'good examples,' and 'what further structure can be extracted' should be phrased more narrowly as wanting to know more about that specific algebra. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))
refined_question: For oriented virtual links considered up to generalized Reidemeister equivalence, is the fundamental biquandle BQ(K) a complete invariant up to mirror images, with the explicit caveat that the authors already know BQ takes the same value on the orientation-reversed mirror image obtained by reflecting in a plane perpendicular to the diagram plane; can one exhibit good examples of biquandles that satisfy the Section 3.2 axioms but are not strong, in the sense that the elements x, y, z, t required in axiom (3) exist but are not uniquely determined; and, in the linear case coming from the Alexander biquandle, what more can be understood about the algebra with generators A and B and relation [B,(A - 1)(A, B)] = 0 cited in [5]? ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))
justification: This is the right target because Problem 10 in Section 7 states these three questions consecutively and almost in the same words as your draft. Section 3.2 provides the needed definitions of the fundamental biquandle and of 'strong' biquandle, while Section 3.3 gives the paper's linear/Alexander biquandle context. The only substantial additions needed to make your draft fully stand-alone are the construction of BQ(K), the exact mirror-image caveat, the meaning of 'strong,' and the ring-theoretic hypotheses attached in the cited source [5] to the algebra [B,(A - 1)(A, B)] = 0. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))
